title: MSbar restoration of the first two rotating Hessian Born terms
matching: Original Candidate 1, g=.1, a=1,b=.1,Omega from original profile, mu/(g*v)=1. No finite counterterm adjustment.
units: The output is the one-loop Routhian divided by g*v. Classical energy divided by g*v is Ebar/g². A fixed-Q interpretation requires the separate charge/collective-coordinate derivation.

potentials.C: bF², rotating traceless X matrix with harmonics +/-2Omega

second_graph: -1/(64pi²)*int_0∞ dk k²/(2pi²) [Atilde² B0(-k²;2,2)+2Btilde² B0(-k²;1,1)+2Ctilde² B0(4Omega²-k²;1,1)+2Dtilde² B0(Omega²-k²;2,1)+Etilde² B0(-k²;1.01,1.01)]
Fourier: Vtilde(k)=4pi int_0∞dr r² sinc(k*r) V(r); real radial functions
B0: -int_0^1 dx log([x m1²+(1-x)m2²-x(1-x)s]/mu²), mu²=1 in these units
spatial_integration: Composite Simpson; Fourier transform in blocks <=256 momenta to bound memory

checks.Parseval: int dk k² |Vtilde|²/(2pi²) agrees with int d³r V² for all5 potentials on finest momentum grid within relative1e-7
checks.radial_convergence: Restored second graph differs between prescribed radial refinements by <1e-4 in output units
checks.momentum_convergence: Second graph difference K40→80 <1e-4 in output units; report rather than hide any failure
checks.Feynman_convergence: 32,64,128 node differences are reported; finest64→128 total change <1e-5
checks.cuts: All5 kernels have positive Feynman denominators at k=0; larger k increases denominator
checks.RG_derivative: At fixed matching parameters explicit d(K1graph+K2graph)/dlnmu=-int tr[(Hvac+DeltaV)²-Hvac²]/(32pi²). Evaluate graph totals at mu/(gv)=1/2,1,2 and compare derivative within1e-6. This checks local MSbar counterterm restoration, not a full energy RG prediction.
checks.loop_order: Only first and second terms of Hessian-potential logdet expansion. They are not a complete one-loop soliton energy on their own.

diagnostics: Compute Vmax from the full4real profile ΔV and I2=intd³r trΔV² for a full-angular UV remainder bound. A numerical sup is not an interval-certified profile bound.
gravity: Vacuum subtraction defines relative matter energy. It does not calibrate the gravitating total constant or cancel the preceding raw scalar vacuum shift.
